text: Tobacco use, including smoking, remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in Ontario. Despite substantial declines in smoking, further reductions have stalled. Some populations continue to smoke at high rates and need support to quit. Further, many people are routinely exposed to secondhand smoke in their homes. Provincial action on tobacco control is guided by the Smoke-Free Ontario Strategy (SFOS), which is funded by the Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care (MOHLTC) and will be renewed in 2018. In preparation, the MOHLTC has released a consultation report, Smoke-Free Ontario Modernization: Report of the Executive Steering Committee, which will be the basis of a renewed SFOS and proposes achieving an 'end-game' smoking rate below 5 percent by 2035 by taking action in five strategic areas: challenging and containing the tobacco industry, motivating and supporting smokers to…

The Board of Health: 1. Endorsed, in principle, the recommendations in the Smoke-Free Ontario Modernization: Report of the Executive Steering Committee report and endorsed the proposed target of reducing smoking prevalence to below 5 percent by 2035 for Ontario. 2. Requested the Government of Ontario to commit in achieving a smoking prevalence below 5 percent by 2035 by executing the strategy outlined in the report Smoke-Free Ontario Modernization: Report of the Executive Steering Committee, in consultation with stakeholders, including public health units. 3. Directed that a copy of the report (December 20, 2017) from the Medical Officer of Health be forwarded to the Premier of Ontario, the Minister of Health and Long-Term Care, and the Co-Chairs of the Executive Steering Committee for the Modernization of Smoke-Free Ontario.
